title: The invalid-address case now reaches unsafe frame access
text:
### The invalid-address case now reaches unsafe frame access

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`
- **Location:** `lock-protocol/src/test/rw_version/exec/cursor.rs:527`
- **Evidence:** Before the patch, lines 507–509 were executable control flow: `if pa == INVALID_PADDR { continue; }`. After the patch, this is `assert(pa != INVALID_PADDR) by { admit(); };`, followed by `allocator.get_pt_frame_from_pa(pa)` at line 534 and `unsafe { frame.page_table_frame.deref() }` at line 535.
- **Problem:** An admitted `assert` is proof-only and cannot replace the removed runtime branch. When the atomic load returns `INVALID_PADDR`, execution no longer retries; it instead treats the sentinel as a valid physical address and proceeds to indexing and unsafe dereference. This is a concrete behavior and safety regression, not merely proof debt.
- **Suggestion:** Restore the executable `if pa == INVALID_PADDR { continue; }` path (or implement another explicit runtime retry/error path). Prove the subsequent validity facts only on the non-sentinel branch; do not use `admit()` to erase a reachable runtime case.

title: Enabling `rw_version::exec` makes admitted facts part of the active verification boundary
text:
### Enabling `rw_version::exec` makes admitted facts part of the active verification boundary

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Locations:** `lock-protocol/src/test/rw_version/mod.rs:1`; `lock-protocol/src/test/rw_version/exec/cursor.rs:213`; `lock-protocol/src/helpers/bits.rs:6`
- **Evidence:** The patch changes the previously commented `// pub mod exec;` to `pub mod exec;`. In that now-active module it adds `assert(tree_path.len() < 3) by { admit(); };` at `cursor.rs:213`, adds further admitted facts at lines 457–458, 527, 624, 638–642, and 650–654, and retains many other admits. It also adds a generally visible helper annotated `#[verifier::external_body]` whose contract asserts `res == low_bits_mask(k as nat)`.
- **Problem:** Activating this module turns its admits into dependencies of public verified APIs such as `lock_range`, while the new bit-mask helper introduces another trusted fact in a general `helpers` module. These assumptions are scattered through caller code rather than confined to a reviewed external/trust boundary, so successful verification would overstate what has actually been proved.
- **Suggestion:** Keep the executable module disabled until the newly relied-on facts are proved, or explicitly isolate the unfinished prototype. Replace local admits with lemmas derived from the model invariants. If the bit-mask bridge truly cannot be verified directly or reused, move the minimal external specification into the project’s centralized external-spec boundary and document the exact tool limitation; otherwise prove the implementation and remove `external_body`.

title: H1 — `PreemptDisabled` no longer disables preemption, so the enabled `RwArc` can self-deadlock on a preemptible CPU
text:
### H1 — `PreemptDisabled` no longer disables preemption, so the enabled `RwArc` can self-deadlock on a preemptible CPU

**Evidence:** `ostd/src/sync/guard.rs:34-53` still documents `PreemptDisabled` as “disabl[ing] preemption while holding a lock”, but changes both associated guard types from `DisabledPreemptGuard` to `()` and changes `guard()` / `read_guard()` from `disable_preempt()` to `()`. The same patch enables `rwarc` in `ostd/src/sync/mod.rs:6,18`, and `ostd/src/sync/rwarc.rs:30-32` selects `RwLock<T, PreemptDisabled>`. `RwLock::try_read`, `try_write`, and `try_upread` retain the guardian in their returned lock guards (`ostd/src/sync/rwlock.rs:389,445,479` and `603-606,678-682`), showing that the guardian lifetime is intended to cover the lock-holding interval.

**Impact:** a task can be preempted while holding this spin-based `RwLock`; if another task scheduled on the same CPU tries to take the conflicting lock, it spins while the holder cannot run. This is a runtime liveness/safety regression, not merely a missing proof annotation. It also contradicts the public type documentation and the `SpinGuardian` invariant that atomic mode is maintained while the lock is held (`guard.rs:4-6`).

**Required correction:** restore `DisabledPreemptGuard` and calls to `disable_preempt()` before exporting `PreemptDisabled` or enabling `RwArc`. If that implementation cannot yet be verified, keep the executable behavior intact behind a narrowly justified trust boundary; do not replace the behavior with a verification-friendly no-op.

title: M1 — The newly exposed `RwArc` API is almost entirely trusted and has no usable functional contracts
text:
### M1 — The newly exposed `RwArc` API is almost entirely trusted and has no usable functional contracts

**Evidence:** the patch enables and publicly re-exports `RwArc` / `RoArc` (`ostd/src/sync/mod.rs:6,18`) while adding `#[verifier::external_body]` to `RwArc::new`, `read`, `write`, `get`, `clone_ro`, `Clone::clone`, `Drop::drop`, `get_cloned`, and `RoArc::read` (`ostd/src/sync/rwarc.rs:37-38,47-48,53-54,67-68,84-85,92-93,105-110,116-117,125-126`). None states preconditions or postconditions connecting the result to the input value, the protected allocation, the read/write capability, or the `num_rw` uniqueness condition. The helper used to manufacture the reference in `get` is also trusted (`ostd/src/sync/rwlock.rs:553-563`).

**Impact:** verification accepts the most safety-sensitive bodies—including the unsafe reference construction and reference-count bookkeeping—without checking them, while verified callers receive essentially no semantic API contract. This creates a broad trust island exactly at the ownership/aliasing boundary and prevents callers from establishing even basic facts such as `new(x)` protecting `x`, a read guard observing the same allocation, or `get()` returning that allocation's value when uniqueness holds.

**Required correction:** define a stable abstract model for allocation identity, protected value, and read/write capability; give each public method a contract over that model; then minimize trusted code to the primitive operations that genuinely cannot be verified. In particular, specify and justify the invariant relating `num_rw` to live `RwArc` handles before trusting `get`, `clone`, and `drop` as a group.

title: M2 — The only focused `RwArc` regression test is disabled in the same change that enables the module
text:
### M2 — The only focused `RwArc` regression test is disabled in the same change that enables the module

**Evidence:** `ostd/src/sync/rwarc.rs:132-150` comments out the complete `#[cfg(ktest)]` test module. The removed test exercised the key `num_rw` transition: `get()` succeeds for one `RwArc`, fails after cloning another `RwArc`, and succeeds again after dropping that clone. Meanwhile the patch changes `rwarc` from disabled to compiled and publicly exported in `ostd/src/sync/mod.rs`.

**Impact:** the newly activated ownership/counting path loses its direct regression check, including the acquire/release handoff on which lockless `get()` relies. This makes the broad `external_body` trust boundary in M1 harder to audit and allows runtime behavior to diverge from the intended uniqueness invariant unnoticed.

**Required correction:** keep the focused kernel test active (adapting its placement or annotations for the Verus build if necessary) and add a guardian-behavior test or assertion that demonstrates preemption remains disabled for the full lifetime of guards using `PreemptDisabled`.

title: The new write-lock invariant is trusted rather than proved
text:
### The new write-lock invariant is trusted rather than proved

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Location:** `lock-protocol/src/test/rw_version/spec/tree.rs:475`
- **Evidence:**

  ```rust
  assert(post.inv_write_lock_cursors_subtree_locked()) by {
     admit();
  }
  ```

  The patch changes the inductiveness obligation from `post.inv_non_overlapping()` to the stronger, newly introduced `post.inv_write_lock_cursors_subtree_locked()`, but continues to discharge the changed obligation with `admit()`. This invariant states that every write-lock cursor points to a `WriteLocked` node whose descendants have neither readers nor write locks; trusting it bypasses the core exclusion property that the PR is restructuring.

  **Suggestion:** Prove `post.inv_write_lock_cursors_subtree_locked()` from the `write_lock` transition requirements and the pre-state invariants. In particular, establish that the selected node has zero readers and that no descendant is read- or write-locked, then use the cursor update lemmas to preserve the predicate for all other cursors. Do not keep this proof debt in an inductiveness check.

title: A new subtree/accounting theorem is introduced with `admit()`
text:
### A new subtree/accounting theorem is introduced with `admit()`

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Location:** `lock-protocol/src/test/rw_version/spec/tree.rs:588`
- **Evidence:**

  ```rust
  proof fn lemma_read_counter_zero_implies_subtree_zero(&self, nid: NodeId, child: NodeId)
  ...
  ensures
      self.reader_counts[child] == 0,
  {
      ...
      admit();
  }
  ```

  This is a new logical fact about reader-count propagation, and its unchecked postcondition becomes available to later proofs even though the current patch does not derive it. The commented-out proof sketch immediately above the `admit()` does not constrain that trusted fact.

  **Suggestion:** Complete the contradiction proof: if `child` has a positive count, use `inv_reader_counts_cursors_relation` to obtain a cursor whose read path contains `child`, use the cursor/path invariant plus `in_subtree_range(nid, child)` to show that the same path contains `nid`, and derive a positive count for `nid`. If that implication needs an additional path-ordering premise, add it explicitly rather than admitting the stronger theorem.

title: The insertion lemmas do not provide the documented construction direction
text:
### The insertion lemmas do not provide the documented construction direction

- **Guideline:** `api-postconditions`
- **Locations:** `vstd_extra/src/map_extra.rs:250`, `vstd_extra/src/map_extra.rs:279`
- **Evidence:** The documentation says that the inserted-map property “holds if” the old-map property and the inserted value's predicate hold, but both contracts state only the converse:

  ```rust
  /// `forall_map(m.insert(k, v), f)` holds if `f(k, v)` holds and ...
  ensures
      forall_map(m.insert(k, v), f) ==> f(k, v) && ...

  /// `forall_map_values(m.insert(k, v), f)` holds if `f(v)` holds and ...
  ensures
      forall_map_values(m.insert(k, v), f) ==> f(v) && ...
  ```

  Thus a natural caller that knows `f(k, v)`/`f(v)` and the appropriate old-map predicate cannot derive `forall_map(m.insert(k, v), f)` or `forall_map_values(m.insert(k, v), f)`. That is the direction needed to preserve a universal map invariant across insertion and the direction explicitly promised by the API comments.

  **Suggestion:** Make each postcondition an equivalence, matching the neighboring remove lemmas, or add the missing forward implication as a separate `ensures` clause and prove it. For example, use `forall_map(m.insert(k, v), f) <==> f(k, v) && if m.contains_key(k) { forall_map(m.remove(k), f) } else { forall_map(m, f) }`, with the analogous value-only form.

title: The verification change removes the core `RwArc` API and leaves its enabled test uncompilable
text:
### The verification change removes the core `RwArc` API and leaves its enabled test uncompilable

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/sync/rwarc.rs:66`
- **Quoted evidence:** The after-image starts a block comment immediately before `pub fn get` (`/*` at line 66), closes it after `get_cloned` at line 130, and therefore excludes `get`, `impl Clone for RwArc<T>`, `impl Drop for RwArc<T>`, and `get_cloned` from compilation. At the same time, lines 142-159 enable `#[cfg(ktest)]` code that calls `rw1.get()`, `rw1.clone()`, and `drop(rw2)`. The retained public rustdoc at lines 22-25 also says the type exists to provide lockless access and links to the now-absent `RwArc::get` method.
- **Problem:** This is a caller-visible behavioral and source-compatibility regression, not a proof-only refactoring. Under `ktest`, method resolution for `get` and `clone` has no corresponding compiled implementation; outside tests, downstream callers lose those public operations and `num_rw` no longer tracks multiple `RwArc` owners because the only increment/decrement implementations were commented out.
- **Suggestion:** Remove the block comments, retain the original `get`, `Clone`, `Drop`, and `get_cloned` executable code, and model the atomic counter transitions needed to verify those implementations. If some operations cannot yet be proved, keep their executable bodies and use a narrow, explicitly documented temporary verification boundary rather than deleting the API from the compiled program. Keep the test enabled only once it compiles against the restored API.

title: H1 — Re-enabled wait/IRQ APIs depend on removed runtime behavior
text:
### H1 — Re-enabled wait/IRQ APIs depend on removed runtime behavior

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`
- **Locations:** `ostd/src/arch/x86/irq.rs:86`, `ostd/src/sync/wait.rs:192`, `ostd/src/task/scheduler/mod.rs:86`, `ostd/src/task/scheduler/mod.rs:547`, `ostd/src/trap/irq.rs:256`
- **Quoted evidence:** `arch/x86/irq.rs` changes both `disable_local` and `is_local_enabled` from real x86 operations to `unimplemented!()` (lines 86–93). `Waiter::new_pair` replaces `Task::current().unwrap().cloned()` with `Arc::new(Task {})` (wait.rs:192–197), while `Waker::wake_up` still passes that task to `scheduler::unpark_target` (lines 282–289). `inject_scheduler` now has an empty body because `SCHEDULER.call_once(...)` and timer registration are block-commented (scheduler/mod.rs:86–97), and `reschedule` computes `next_task` but comments out `processor::switch_to_task(next_task)` (lines 547–580). Finally, the `Drop` implementation that re-enabled IRQs when `was_enabled` is true is block-commented (trap/irq.rs:256–262), although `disable_local` still documents automatic restoration on drop (lines 198–202).
- **Problem:** These are observable semantic deletions, not proof-only changes. Constructing an IRQ guard immediately panics; if those stubs were filled, dropping the guard would still no longer restore interrupts. The wait path associates its waker with a fabricated empty task, scheduler injection cannot initialize `SCHEDULER`, and a reschedule decision never performs a context switch. The newly exported `WaitQueue`, `Waiter`, and `Waker` therefore cannot satisfy their existing runtime documentation.
- **Suggestion:** Restore the original executable IRQ, task identity, scheduler initialization/context-switch, and guard `Drop` implementations verbatim before adding verification annotations. Isolate any not-yet-verifiable body at the verification boundary without changing what runs, and enable one dependency-complete slice at a time.

title: H2 — `DerefMut` fabricates an `UnsafeCell<T>` view of a `PCell<T>`
text:
### H2 — `DerefMut` fabricates an `UnsafeCell<T>` view of a `PCell<T>`

- **Guidelines:** `preserve-exec-code`, `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/sync/spin.rs:448`
- **Quoted evidence:** The new implementation performs `let ucell: *const UnsafeCell<T> = (&self.lock.inner.val as *const PCell<T>).cast();` followed by `&mut *(*ucell).get()` (lines 448–454). The adjacent verified immutable `Deref` instead obtains a tracked permission and calls `self.lock.inner.val.borrow(Tracked(read_perm))` (lines 432–443). No layout equivalence between `PCell<T>` and `UnsafeCell<T>` or mutable permission is established in the patch.
- **Problem:** A raw-pointer cast does not establish that two unrelated wrapper types have the same representation, and it bypasses `PCell`'s permission discipline to create a mutable reference. This changes a lock guard's core unsafe access path without a stated or checked representation/synchronization argument, so it can invalidate both Rust aliasing safety and the verified ownership model.
- **Suggestion:** Implement mutable access through `PCell`'s supported mutable-borrow API using the guard's tracked write permission, analogous to the immutable `borrow` path. If an unavoidable external bridge is required, put the smallest bridge in the repository's explicit external boundary and state the exact layout, exclusivity, and lifetime conditions; do not reinterpret the field inline.

title: M1 — The enabled wait/guard surface is accepted through local trusted bodies
text:
### M1 — The enabled wait/guard surface is accepted through local trusted bodies

- **Guidelines:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`, `complete-external-contracts`
- **Locations:** `ostd/src/sync/wait.rs:54`, `ostd/src/sync/wait.rs:191`, `ostd/src/sync/wait.rs:261`, `ostd/src/sync/guard.rs:102`
- **Quoted evidence:** The patch adds 23 `#[verifier::external_body]` occurrences: the external type wrapper plus guard methods, and essentially every constructor, wait, wake, enqueue, access, drop, and helper body newly enabled in `sync/wait.rs`. For example, `WaitQueue::wait_until` (wait.rs:73–90), `Waiter::new_pair` (191–202), `Waiter::drop` (260–269), and `Waker::wake_up` (282–290) are all trusted. None of these APIs gains a `requires`/`ensures` contract in the patch.
- **Problem:** Verification does not check the newly activated concurrency and lifecycle logic, and verified callers receive no useful state-transition or wake-delivery facts from it. Keeping these trusted annotations beside ordinary callers also obscures which minimal OS/atomic behaviors are actually intended to be trusted, especially while the bodies contain the runtime substitutions in H1.
- **Suggestion:** Restore correct executable behavior first, specify the minimal caller-visible queue/waker and guard properties, and verify the ordinary coordination logic. Centralize only irreducible architecture/atomic models in the established external-specification layer with complete contracts; remove local `external_body` annotations from deterministic wrappers and protocol code.

title: The patch removes `RwArc` and `RoArc` from the compiled public API
text:
### The patch removes `RwArc` and `RoArc` from the compiled public API

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/sync/mod.rs:6`, `ostd/src/sync/mod.rs:16`
- **Quoted evidence:** Before the patch, the module contains `mod rwarc;` and publicly re-exports `rwarc::{RoArc, RwArc}`. The after-image changes those exact declarations to `//mod rwarc;` and `//rwarc::{RoArc, RwArc},`. The implementation still exists in `ostd/src/sync/rwarc.rs`, but it is no longer compiled or reachable through `ostd::sync`.
- **Problem:** This is an executable and source-compatibility regression, not a proof-only refactoring. Every downstream import or use of `ostd::sync::{RwArc, RoArc}` loses the types entirely, including all of their runtime behavior.
- **Suggestion:** Keep `mod rwarc;` and the `pub use` entry active. If the rewritten `RwLock` proof representation temporarily prevents `rwarc.rs` from verifying, preserve the executable API behind a narrow, documented verification boundary rather than removing the module from compilation.

title: The rewritten `RwLock` module has invalid `impl` syntax
text:
### The rewritten `RwLock` module has invalid `impl` syntax

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/sync/rwlock.rs:694`, `ostd/src/sync/rwlock.rs:699`, `ostd/src/sync/rwlock.rs:704`
- **Quoted evidence:** The patch changes all three negative auto-trait implementations to `impl<T /*?Sized*/,, G: SpinGuardian> !Send ...`, with two consecutive commas in the generic parameter list: one each for `RwLockWriteGuard`, `RwLockReadGuard`, and `RwLockUpgradeableGuard`.
- **Problem:** A generic parameter list cannot contain an empty parameter between two commas. These active declarations therefore prevent `rwlock.rs` from parsing, so neither Rust compilation nor Verus verification can reach the new invariant and ghost-resource proofs.
- **Suggestion:** Remove the extra comma in each declaration, yielding `impl<T /*?Sized*/, G: SpinGuardian> !Send ...`, and run the normal formatter/build/verification checks after the correction.

title: The trusted traversal contract excludes an executable `None` result
text:
### The trusted traversal contract excludes an executable `None` result

- **Guidelines:** `complete-external-contracts`, `api-postconditions`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/locking.rs:166`
- **Evidence:** The changed `#[verifier::external_body]` contract unconditionally adds `r is Some` (`locking.rs:166`). The same function's rustdoc says that on a stray locked node "it will return `None`. The caller should retry" (`locking.rs:155-157`), and its executable body still contains `if is_stray { return None; }` (`locking.rs:327-329`). `lock_range` then replaces `assert(subtree_root is Some) by { admit() }` with a bare assertion (`locking.rs:83`), so the new trusted postcondition is exactly what discharges the former admit.
- **Problem:** The external-body contract contradicts a reachable result that the function explicitly implements. Verification can therefore reason past the retry case and unwrap the result using a false trusted fact; this is not a proof of the old obligation.
- **Suggestion:** Do not promise `r is Some`. Preserve the documented `Option` behavior, restore the retry loop in `lock_range` (or prove from explicit, truthful preconditions that the stray case is impossible), and give the helper conditional postconditions for both `Some` and `None` outcomes.

title: The split proof fabricates a slot permission and unrelated region facts
text:
### The split proof fabricates a slot permission and unrelated region facts

- **Guidelines:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`, `complete-external-contracts`
- **Location:** `ostd/specs/mm/page_table/node/entry_owners.rs:104`
- **Evidence:** `placeholder_slot_perm` remains a public axiom that returns a tracked `PointsTo<MetaSlot>` without consuming it from `regions.slots`; the patch strengthens it to guarantee initialization, `wf`, non-`UNUSED` refcount, and `path_if_in_pt is None` (`entry_owners.rs:104-114`). Its only new semantic precondition is `regions.inv()` plus address bounds/alignment. But `MetaRegionOwners::inv` guarantees only `MetaSlotOwner::inv()` for every `slot_owners` entry and relates a `PointsTo` value to the owner only when the index is present in `regions.slots` (`ostd/specs/mm/frame/meta_region_owners.rs:57-83`); it does not imply non-`UNUSED` or `path_if_in_pt is None`. The split calls the axiom at `ostd/src/mm/page_table/node/entry.rs:780` and immediately uses the newly asserted region facts at lines 805-821 to replace prior admits.
- **Problem:** The axiom can be called for any aligned in-range address, including a slot whose real permission remains in `regions.slots` or whose owner has a different path/refcount state. It both duplicates a linear ownership capability and asserts state facts not entailed by its preconditions, making the resulting `Child::Frame` invariant trusted rather than verified.
- **Suggestion:** Remove `placeholder_slot_perm` from this path. Split the huge-frame ownership representation so the real child `PointsTo<MetaSlot>` permissions are derived/partitioned and threaded into each child, with the required refcount/path facts proved from that operation. If a temporary trust boundary is unavoidable, place a narrowly scoped boundary in the ownership module and require the exact permission/state facts as inputs instead of asserting them as outputs.

title: `lock_range` no longer exposes the invariant its sole wrapper promises
text:
### `lock_range` no longer exposes the invariant its sole wrapper promises

- **Guideline:** `api-postconditions`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/locking.rs:43`
- **Evidence:** The old contract guaranteed `ret.0.invariants(*ret.1, *regions, *guards)`, `ret.1.in_locked_range()`, and `ret.0.level < ret.0.guard_level`; the patch deletes all three and retains only `ret.0.level <= ret.0.guard_level` plus address/frame properties (`locking.rs:43-55`). The sole call at `ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/mod.rs:264-266` is the success result of public `Cursor::new`, whose contract still promises those deleted invariant, locked-range, and strict-level facts (`cursor/mod.rs:226-234`).
- **Problem:** The callee's callable contract no longer connects its returned `CursorOwner` to `regions` or `guards`, so a caller cannot establish the natural cursor invariant or the wrapper's still-advertised success contract from `lock_range`'s postconditions. Weakening the internal API contract also hides the central result of acquiring the range lock.
- **Suggestion:** Restore the relational invariant, `in_locked_range`, and strict-level postconditions on `lock_range`, and prove them using truthful contracts for the traversal/DFS helpers. If the algorithm can legitimately return at the guard level, change the outer API and its documented semantics consistently rather than weakening only the helper.

title: `placeholder_slot_perm` manufactures ownership and arbitrary region facts
text:
### `placeholder_slot_perm` manufactures ownership and arbitrary region facts

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Location:** `ostd/specs/mm/page_table/node/entry_owners.rs:104`
- **Evidence:** The changed axiom takes only a shared tracked borrow and requires only `regions.inv()`, address alignment, and an address bound, but returns a fresh linear permission and now ensures:

  ```rust
  pub axiom fn placeholder_slot_perm(paddr: Paddr, tracked regions: &MetaRegionOwners)
      -> (tracked res: PointsTo<MetaSlot>)
      requires regions.inv(), paddr % PAGE_SIZE == 0, paddr < MAX_PADDR,
      ensures
          res.is_init(),
          res.value().wf(regions.slot_owners[frame_to_index(paddr)]),
          regions.slot_owners[frame_to_index(paddr)].inner_perms.ref_count.value() != REF_COUNT_UNUSED,
          regions.slot_owners[frame_to_index(paddr)].path_if_in_pt is None;
  ```

  By contrast, `MetaRegionOwners::inv` only connects a real slot permission to its owner under `self.slots.contains_key(i)` (`ostd/specs/mm/frame/meta_region_owners.rs:64-75`); it does not state that every slot is non-`UNUSED` or has no page-table path. The caller then uses exactly the newly manufactured facts at `ostd/src/mm/page_table/node/entry.rs:780-821` to construct `child_owner` and discharge `Child::Frame(...).invariants(...)`.
- **Problem:** A shared borrow cannot transfer a unique `PointsTo` out of `regions`, and the preconditions do not imply the two asserted `slot_owners` facts. Repeated calls can also obtain multiple permissions for the same address, while a permission may still be present in `regions.slots`. Consequently, the axiom can establish the split invariant regardless of the actual allocator/metadata state, so the removed local admits have merely been replaced by a stronger global trust hole.
- **Suggestion:** Remove this placeholder axiom. During huge-page splitting, thread or split the real metadata-slot permissions through `MetaRegionOwners`, consuming/removing each permission from `regions.slots` (or use an existing ownership operation that does so), and derive `is_init`, `wf`, reference-count, and `path_if_in_pt` facts from that concrete ownership transition. If that ownership model is not implemented yet, keep the split path explicitly unverified rather than granting these facts for every aligned address.

title: The new absent-PTE law is supplied only by an admitted implementation
text:
### The new absent-PTE law is supplied only by an admitted implementation

- **Guideline:** `complete-external-contracts`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/mm/page_table/mod.rs:338`
- **Evidence:** The patch strengthens `PageTableEntryTrait::new_properties` with:

  ```rust
  forall|level: PagingLevel|
      1 < level ==> !Self::new_absent_spec().is_last(level),
  ```

  This fact is used by `EntryOwner::absent_match_pte` (`ostd/specs/mm/page_table/node/entry_owners.rs:165-179`) and ultimately by the split proof. The only implementation remains:

  ```rust
  proof fn new_properties()
  {
      admit();
  }
  ```

  at `ostd/specs/arch/x86_64/page_table_entry.rs:315-318`. Nearby executable/spec definitions show `is_last(level)` is `level == 1 || HUGE-bit-is-set` (`:300-307`), so this particular new law should be derivable for the zero-valued absent PTE.
- **Problem:** Adding a postcondition to an already admitted proof expands the facts accepted on trust. The patch therefore relies on a newly trusted representation law even though the representation definition appears sufficient to prove it directly.
- **Suggestion:** Implement `new_properties` (or at least factor and prove the absent-PTE lemma from `new_absent_spec` and `is_last_spec`) so the newly added guarantee is checked against the actual PTE encoding. Keep any genuinely external facts at a narrowly documented boundary.

title: DMA platform detection and device mapping were replaced by stubs
text:
### DMA platform detection and device mapping were replaced by stubs

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/mm/dma/mod.rs:131`; `ostd/src/mm/dma/dma_stream.rs:152`
- **Evidence:** The new detector is `#[verifier::external_body] pub fn dma_type() -> DmaType { unimplemented!() }`. In the new `DmaType::Iommu` branch, the loop computes `paddr` but the former `iommu::map(paddr as Daddr, paddr).unwrap()` call is only represented by the comment `// iommu::map...`. The base implementation queried `has_dma_remapping()`, performed the IOMMU map, and performed the x86 TDX unprotect operation.
- **Problem:** Every call to `DmaStream::map` reaches `dma_type()` and panics at runtime. Even after replacing that panic, both the IOMMU mapping and the TDX transition have been removed, so the returned device address does not denote the mapping promised by the API.
- **Suggestion:** Restore the original executable detector and both architecture-specific mapping paths unchanged, then specify those operations at their existing boundaries. If a specific call cannot yet be verified, retain the working executable call and isolate only its specification/trust obligation; do not replace runtime behavior with `unimplemented!()` or comments.

title: The DMA overlap registry no longer records mappings
text:
### The DMA overlap registry no longer records mappings

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/mm/dma/mod.rs:89`
- **Evidence:** The second loop computes `let paddr = ...`, but `mapping_set.insert(paddr)` is commented out at lines 121-122, after which the function returns `true`. The base implementation inserted every address. The patch also removes `remove_dma_mapping` and the `Drop for DmaStreamInner` implementation that released the registered range and tore down the device mapping.
- **Problem:** Two live streams over the same physical frames can both pass `check_and_insert_dma_mapping`, contradicting the documented `AlreadyMapped` behavior and the exclusivity invariant this set is meant to enforce. Removing teardown also loses the lifecycle symmetry needed once insertion is restored.
- **Suggestion:** Keep the original insert/remove and `Drop` behavior executable. Add the ghost model needed to prove that a successful insertion reserves the whole page range until the final inner owner is dropped, without deleting either side of the runtime lifecycle.

title: All permitted DMA reads and writes now fail
text:
### All permitted DMA reads and writes now fail

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`, `api-postconditions`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/mm/dma/dma_stream.rs:343`; `ostd/src/mm/dma/dma_stream.rs:371`
- **Evidence:** After the direction and bounds checks, `read_inner_vmio` unconditionally executes `Err(Error::InvalidArgs)` at line 359, and `write_inner_vmio` does the same at line 387. The base implementation delegated valid operations to `self.inner.segment.read(offset, writer)` and `.write(offset, reader)`.
- **Problem:** The `VmIo` implementation cannot perform any successful transfer, including valid in-range operations in the permitted direction. This directly contradicts the trait documentation's read/write purpose and its no-short-success behavior.
- **Suggestion:** Restore delegation to the segment after the direction checks (and preserve the original offset semantics). Give the helper and trait implementation postconditions that state the success case's cursor/owner updates and error case's frame conditions.

title: Trusted functions can fabricate memory-view ownership from shared metadata
text:
### Trusted functions can fabricate memory-view ownership from shared metadata

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`, `complete-external-contracts`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/mm/frame/segment.rs:172`; `ostd/src/mm/frame/segment.rs:188`; `ostd/src/mm/io.rs:413`
- **Evidence:** `produce_kernel_mem_view` takes only `tracked &self` and returns an owned `tracked view: MemView` from `arbitrary()`; it can therefore be called repeatedly from the same shared `SegmentOwner`. `borrow_kernel_mem_view` likewise returns an arbitrary tracked reference. Separately, `VmIoOwner::advance` was changed from a checked `MemView::split`/`borrow_at` implementation to `#[verifier::external_body] ... { arbitrary() }`, and its `res` does not occur in any `ensures` clause despite the documentation claiming it is the advanced portion.
- **Problem:** These are local, generic trust boundaries for the memory permission that justifies reads and writes. In particular, a shared `&SegmentOwner` can manufacture multiple owned views of the same segment, while `advance` can return an unrelated tracked view; the contracts do not encode a transfer, split, or borrow relationship that prevents aliasing of write authority.
- **Suggestion:** Restore the checked `advance` implementation and specify `res` as precisely the removed prefix. Derive segment views from the actual frame-content ownership: consume or mutably split ownership for a writable view, and tie a read borrow's lifetime and model to the source owner. If an unavoidable architecture axiom remains, centralize the narrow external specification in the established external-spec boundary rather than exposing generic `external_body` constructors in `ostd/src`.

title: `VmIo`'s enabled DMA contract does not constrain any observable output
text:
### `VmIo`'s enabled DMA contract does not constrain any observable output

- **Guideline:** `api-postconditions`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/mm/dma/dma_stream.rs:424`; `ostd/src/mm/dma/dma_stream.rs:458`; `ostd/src/mm/io.rs:1075`
- **Evidence:** The implementation sets both `obeys_vmio_read_spec()` and `obeys_vmio_write_spec()` to `true`, but its `read_spec` and `write_spec` bodies are only `self.inv()`. `DmaStream::inv()` itself is `true` at lines 94-97. Thus the trait `ensures` at `io.rs:1090-1101` and `io.rs:1126-1137` says nothing about `r`, the final reader/writer, either final `VmIoOwner`, or the final stream owner.
- **Problem:** Even after the runtime bodies are repaired, verified callers cannot establish that success transfers all bytes, advances the cursor, updates the memory view, or that failure preserves inputs. The contract therefore fails to expose the trait's documented no-short-read/no-short-write semantics.
- **Suggestion:** Define `read_spec`/`write_spec` over all output positions. At minimum, pin success to full cursor advancement and the corresponding owner/view update, pin failure to the intended frame condition, preserve both owners' invariants and relationships, and connect direction/range failures to the returned error where the API promises those cases.

title: Preserve the original executable paths in the required reviewable form
text:
### Preserve the original executable paths in the required reviewable form

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`
- **Locations:** `ostd/src/mm/frame/unique.rs:133`, `ostd/src/mm/kspace/kvirt_area.rs:450`
- **Evidence:** `UniqueFrame::repurpose` adds an anonymous block containing the former executable sequence, beginning `/* // SAFETY: We are the sole owner and the metadata is initialized.` and ending with `unsafe { core::mem::transmute(self) } */`. The mapping loop likewise adds only `// unsafe { cursor.map(MappedItem::Tracked(frame.into(), prop)) }` / `//     .expect("Failed to map frame in a new `KVirtArea`");`, while execution now goes through `let dynframe = frame_into_dynframe(frame);` and `cursor.map(item)`.
- **Problem:** These are real executable rewrites made for verification, but the preserved originals are not marked `Origin Rust:` and do not state the concrete reason for each rewrite. The VOSTD rule requires an adjacent, concise original-code record and reason so reviewers can check runtime equivalence.
- **Suggestion:** Replace each anonymous commented block with an adjacent `Origin Rust:` block that quotes the exact former executable statement(s) and briefly states the Verus constraint that required the rewrite (tracked metadata ownership for `repurpose`; exposing the conversion model before `cursor.map` for the mapping loop). Keep the rewritten executable path minimal.

title: Inline the one-use invariant bridge instead of expanding the public proof API
text:
### Inline the one-use invariant bridge instead of expanding the public proof API

- **Guidelines:** `inline-single-use-proof-helpers`, `name-proof-roles`
- **Location:** `ostd/specs/mm/frame/unique.rs:111`
- **Evidence:** The patch adds `pub proof fn aligns_with_regions(...)` with an empty body and postconditions equating the region's `inner_perms` and `self_addr` with the owner's fields. Repository search finds exactly one call, at `ostd/src/mm/frame/unique.rs:142`. Its key equalities are already stated by `owner.global_inv(regions)` at `ostd/specs/mm/frame/unique.rs:81-85`. The helper is also a proved reusable fact but is not named with the required `lemma_` prefix.
- **Problem:** This creates a public proof surface for a single local proof step and obscures that the conclusion is a direct consequence of the existing invariant (plus the frame/owner index equalities). The extra `regions.inv()` and unique-reference-count requirements do not contribute to the stated conclusion.
- **Suggestion:** Remove `aligns_with_regions` and prove/assert the index equality and the two `global_inv` conjuncts directly in `UniqueFrame::repurpose`. If a genuine second caller later establishes an abstraction need, reintroduce a narrowly contracted `lemma_*` fact with only the premises used by its conclusion.

title: Consolidate the newly duplicated module import at `ostd/specs/mm/frame/unique.rs:6-7`.
text: | Consolidate the newly duplicated module import at `ostd/specs/mm/frame/unique.rs:6-7`. | `group-imports-by-crate` | The file has both `use super::meta_owners::*;` and the added `use super::meta_owners::REF_COUNT_UNIQUE;`; the glob already brings the constant into scope. Remove the explicit duplicate (or replace the glob with one consolidated explicit import list if that is independently desirable). |

title: Lock guards no longer release the lock on ordinary drop
text:
### Lock guards no longer release the lock on ordinary drop

- **Guideline:** `api-postconditions`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/sync/rwmutex.rs:610`, `:752`, and `:935`
- **Evidence:** The patch removes `impl Drop` for `RwMutexReadGuard_`, `RwMutexWriteGuard_`, and `RwMutexUpgradeableGuard_`, replacing them with inherent methods named `drop(self)`. The resulting file contains no `impl Drop` for any `RwMutex*Guard`. The public documentation still calls these “RAII guards” (`rwmutex.rs:84-87`), says guards are dropped at scope boundaries (`:128`, `:135`), and uses `drop(r1)` / `drop(r2)` (`:119-120`), which invokes `core::mem::drop` rather than an inherent method. The read guard's new inherent `drop` is private as well (`:610`).
- **Problem:** Rust does not call an inherent `drop(self)` method when a value leaves scope. Consequently a normally dropped read, write, or upgradeable guard leaves its lock bit/count held; later acquisitions can block or spin forever, contradicting the central guard API behavior and the examples.
- **Suggestion:** Preserve real `Drop` behavior for executable builds. If current Verus limitations require a manually verified release routine, keep it as a helper and have an actual `Drop::drop` implementation invoke the equivalent release path (using the project's accepted trusted/verified boundary), then add a regression test that reacquires each lock mode after scope exit and after `core::mem::drop`.

title: The write guard no longer provides mutable access
text:
### The write guard no longer provides mutable access

- **Guideline:** `api-postconditions`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/sync/rwmutex.rs:643`
- **Evidence:** The diff deletes the complete `DerefMut for RwMutexWriteGuard_` implementation and adds no replacement; the resulting file has only `Deref for RwMutexWriteGuard` at lines 665-676. Yet the type-level documentation promises “`DerefMut` for the writer” (`:84-86`) and both examples mutate through a write guard with `*w1 += 1` and `*w2 += 1` (`:126`, `:133`).
- **Problem:** `RwMutexWriteGuard` can no longer be used to modify `T`; the documented examples and existing callers that assign through the guard will fail to compile. This removes the defining capability of a write lock while continuing to expose `write`, `upgrade`, and `downgrade` as write-guard APIs.
- **Suggestion:** Restore `DerefMut` with a permission-backed mutable borrow and an accurate Verus contract. If mutable borrowing cannot yet be verified, do not enable/export `RwMutex` as a compatible public replacement until the executable API is preserved, and explicitly isolate any temporary trusted boundary.

title: Reader-count safety is assumed at the atomic invariant boundary
text:
### Reader-count safety is assumed at the atomic invariant boundary

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/sync/rwmutex.rs:394` and `:624`
- **Evidence:** Both the `try_read` increment and read-guard release contain `assume(no_max_reader_overflow(prev_usize));`, where `no_max_reader_overflow(v)` is `v & MAX_READER_MASK < MAX_READER_MASK` (`:243-245`). The new lock invariant equates `total_reader_bits` with active plus failed reader attempts (`:181`) but does not require this strict upper bound; its retract-token capacity is `MAX_READER_MASK + 1` (`:26`, `:45`), so saturation is not excluded by the stated invariant. The assumption is then used by `lemma_consts_properties_value` / `lemma_consts_properties_prev_next` to justify arithmetic and the ghost-state transition.
- **Problem:** The proof accepts the key no-wrap premise instead of deriving it from the lock protocol. This leaves the atomic reader-count transition—and therefore the correspondence between lock bits and permissions—outside the established proof, while presenting the implementation as verified.
- **Suggestion:** Strengthen the invariant/protocol so it proves `v & MAX_READER_MASK < MAX_READER_MASK` whenever `fetch_add(READER)` is permitted, or change the executable transition to reject saturation before incrementing and model that branch. Remove both assumptions and prove the increment/decrement obligations from the invariant and token accounting.

title: Remove the unused trusted mutable-borrow helpers
text:
### Remove the unused trusted mutable-borrow helpers

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`, `reuse-existing-specifications`
- **Location:** `vstd_extra/src/cast_ptr.rs:257`
- **Evidence:** The patch adds:

  ```rust
  #[verifier::external_body]
  pub proof fn borrow_mut_inner_perms(tracked &mut self) -> (tracked result: &mut T::Perm)
  ```

  and, at `vstd_extra/src/cast_ptr.rs:269`:

  ```rust
  #[verifier::external_body]
  pub proof fn borrow_mut_points_to(tracked &mut self) -> (tracked result: &mut simple_pptr::PointsTo<R>)
  ```

  A repository-wide search of the supplied after-tree finds only these definitions, with no call to either helper. Meanwhile the changed caller at `ostd/src/mm/frame/linked_list.rs:972` directly borrows the tracked field:

  ```rust
  slot.in_list.store(Tracked(&mut frame_own.meta_perm.inner_perms.in_list), list_id);
  ```

- **Problem:** Both public helpers ask Verus to trust their contracts despite having no consumer, while the patch itself shows that ordinary tracked-field borrowing suffices for the motivating operation. Keeping unused `external_body` APIs needlessly retains a proof trust boundary and exposes contracts that future proofs could rely on without verification.
- **Suggestion:** Delete both `borrow_mut_inner_perms` and `borrow_mut_points_to`. If a future concrete caller cannot express a required borrow directly, add the narrowest helper at that time and isolate/document the tool limitation at the trusted boundary.

title: 1. `try_traverse_and_lock_subtree_root` promises `Some` although its body still returns `None`
text:
### 1. `try_traverse_and_lock_subtree_root` promises `Some` although its body still returns `None`

**Rules:** `complete-external-contracts`; API postconditions / trusted-boundary soundness.

**Evidence:** [`ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/locking.rs:185`](after/ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/locking.rs#L185) adds the unconditional postcondition `r is Some` to an `#[verifier::external_body]` function. The executable body has two reachable stray-node branches returning `None`, at [`locking.rs:285`](after/ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/locking.rs#L285) and [`locking.rs:338`](after/ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/locking.rs#L338). The function's own documentation immediately above still says that a stray node causes `None` and that the caller should retry. `lock_range` no longer retries and instead unconditionally calls `unwrap()` at [`locking.rs:90`](after/ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/locking.rs#L90).

This is both a false trusted specification and a runtime panic path under the documented stray-node race. The comment claiming that the shipped body is a “post-retry form” does not match the shipped body.

**Suggested correction:** restore `r is Some ==> ...`, restore the retry loop in `lock_range`, and specify/prove the state relation across a `None` result so retries are legal. Alternatively, change the executable external body to actually perform the retry before making `r is Some` unconditional.

title: 1. Child-count safety is asserted by two local axioms instead of represented by the node invariant
text:
### 1. Child-count safety is asserted by two local axioms instead of represented by the node invariant

**Rules:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`; `implement-inv-for-models`.

**Evidence:** [`ostd/specs/mm/page_table/node/owners.rs:136`](after/ostd/specs/mm/page_table/node/owners.rs#L136) and [`owners.rs:147`](after/ostd/specs/mm/page_table/node/owners.rs#L147) add public axioms stating that an absent PTE implies `nr_children < NR_ENTRIES` and a present PTE implies `nr_children > 0`. They are used to justify executable `+ 1` and `- 1` counter updates in `Entry::replace`. The accompanying comment explicitly says the intended invariant is that `nr_children` counts present PTEs, but that invariant is not modeled or maintained; the boundary facts are simply trusted beside their caller.

These axioms can mask drift between the counter and `children_perm`, precisely the relationship needed to justify the arithmetic. Because they are generic over every `PageTableConfig` and have no external implementation whose behavior they specify, they enlarge the trusted logical base.

**Suggested correction:** add the count relationship (or an equivalent inductively maintainable accounting predicate) to `NodeOwner::inv`, establish it at construction, and preserve it at every PTE mutation. Then derive both bounds as ordinary proof lemmas. If temporary trust is unavoidable, isolate and clearly gate it at a dedicated trust boundary rather than exposing generic public axioms on `NodeOwner`.

title: 2. Three changed `rlimit` values exceed the project cap of 200
text:
### 2. Three changed `rlimit` values exceed the project cap of 200

**Rule:** `decompose-before-raising-rlimit`.

**Evidence:** the diff changes/adds `#[verifier::rlimit(10000)]` on [`ostd/specs/mm/page_table/cursor/owners.rs:1142`](after/ostd/specs/mm/page_table/cursor/owners.rs#L1142), `#[verifier::rlimit(1200)]` on [`ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/mod.rs:2519`](after/ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/mod.rs#L2519), and `#[verifier::rlimit(1000)]` on [`cursor/mod.rs:2852`](after/ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/mod.rs#L2852). Each is above the workflow guideline's maximum of 200; two are increases from already excessive values (8000 to 10000 and 400 to 1000).

**Suggested correction:** decompose the affected proofs and keep every changed cap at or below 200.

title: H1 — The tracked/MMIO axiom is inconsistent with the unrestricted frame-owner constructor
text:
### H1 — The tracked/MMIO axiom is inconsistent with the unrestricted frame-owner constructor

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Location:** `ostd/specs/mm/page_table/node/entry_owners.rs:106`, `:124`, `:141`, `:777`
- **Evidence:** `new_frame(..., is_tracked: bool)` has no precondition and returns `Self::new_frame_spec(..., is_tracked)` (`:106-107`). `inv_base` constrains a frame's address, size, level, and shape but never constrains `frame.unwrap().is_tracked` (`:777-806`). Nevertheless, the new broadcast axiom promises for every frame satisfying `inv_base` that `entry.frame.unwrap().is_tracked != is_mmio_paddr(entry.frame.unwrap().mapped_pa)` (`:141-148`). The adjacent `axiom_frame_is_tracked_matches_item` similarly claims a relationship omitted from `inv_base`, and its comment explicitly says the invariant formulation was abandoned because it would require fixing call sites (`:120-123`).
- **Problem:** For any inputs satisfying the address/path/level shape requirements, `new_frame` can construct one `inv_base` owner with `is_tracked = true` and another with `is_tracked = false` at the same `paddr`. Applying `axiom_frame_is_tracked_iff_not_mmio` to both proves respectively `!is_mmio_paddr(paddr)` and `is_mmio_paddr(paddr)`. This makes the proof context inconsistent and allows downstream mapping and allocator-disjointness obligations to be proved from false.
- **Suggestion:** Make trackedness a checked structural invariant. Restrict the constructor with the required relationship (or derive `is_tracked` from the item/address instead of accepting an arbitrary boolean), add the relationship to `inv_base`, and discharge it at every construction and mutation site. Remove both global axioms; the comment's “wide cascading refactor” is the proof obligation, not a sound reason to assume the result.

title: H2 — Child restoration assumes the exact page-table invariant it advertises as proved
text:
### H2 — Child restoration assumes the exact page-table invariant it advertises as proved

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Location:** `ostd/specs/mm/page_table/cursor/owners.rs:393`, `:487`, `:499`
- **Evidence:** `continuation_inv_holds_after_child_restore` promises `self.inv()` (`:393-448`). To establish its `pt_inv_children` component, the new proof handles the restored index with `assume(PageTableOwner(self.children[cont_idx].unwrap()).pt_inv());` (`:487-500`). The preceding comment acknowledges that proving this requires fixing stale path propagation in `alloc_if_none` and adding an operation-specific lemma (`:489-492`).
- **Problem:** The assumption is not an environmental or hardware boundary; it is the missing inductive step for the page-table invariant. Every caller can now obtain `self.inv()` after restoring a child even when that child's paths do not satisfy `pt_inv`, so later verified cursor operations may rely on an invariant that was never established.
- **Suggestion:** Fix child-path propagation and prove an operation-specific `pt_inv` preservation lemma for each restore operation, then pass that proved fact into this helper. Do not expose `self.inv()` until the restored child case is checked, and do not keep the missing invariant as a local assumption.

title: M1 — Safe range operations hide executable overflow behind assumptions
text:
### M1 — Safe range operations hide executable overflow behind assumptions

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/mm/frame/segment.rs:878`, `:881`; `ostd/src/mm/vm_space.rs:852`, `:860`
- **Evidence:** Safe `Segment::slice` says `// KNOWN BUG` and assumes both `self.range.start + range.start <= usize::MAX` and the analogous end bound immediately before performing those additions (`segment.rs:878-886`). Safe `VmSpaceCursor::unmap` likewise assumes `self.pt_cursor.0.va + len <= usize::MAX` immediately before using that addition in an assertion and as `end_va` (`vm_space.rs:852-868`). Neither public contract requires the no-overflow condition; `slice_requires` only constrains frames selected by the resulting mathematical sums (`segment.rs:506-526`), and `unmap` only requires cursor and TLB invariants (`vm_space.rs:838-851`).
- **Problem:** These assumptions let verification ignore reachable arithmetic-overflow behavior in safe executable APIs and use the assumed sums to prove their postconditions. Labeling the condition a known bug identifies rather than justifies the new trusted premise.
- **Suggestion:** Establish the bound from existing cursor/segment invariants and the requested range, or express overflow through a checked addition and the API's documented panic behavior. If the intended caller invariant is genuinely required, add it explicitly to the contract and prove it at callers rather than assuming it inside the body.

title: M2 — Five changed proof limits exceed the workflow cap
text:
### M2 — Five changed proof limits exceed the workflow cap

- **Guideline:** `decompose-before-raising-rlimit`
- **Location:** `ostd/specs/mm/page_table/mod.rs:443`; `ostd/specs/mm/page_table/cursor/owners.rs:1310`, `:1491`; `ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/mod.rs:730`, `:3309`
- **Evidence:** The patch adds or raises limits to `400`, `2000`, `20000`, `800`, and `10000`, respectively. All are greater than the permitted cap of `200`; `node_within_locked_range` is explicitly raised from `10000` to `20000`, and `replace_cur_entry` receives `10000`.
- **Problem:** These limits conceal proof-search blowups instead of decomposing the new arithmetic and cursor-preservation arguments. The largest caps are 50–100 times the workflow limit and make verification substantially less predictable and maintainable.
- **Suggestion:** Split the arithmetic normalization and invariant-preservation steps into focused lemmas, minimize broadcast/reveal scope, and keep each resulting proof at `rlimit <= 200` before merging.

title: Verified mapping and unmapping paths still contain explicit proof holes
text:
### Verified mapping and unmapping paths still contain explicit proof holes

- **Guidelines:** `preserve-exec-code`, `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Locations:** `ostd/src/mm/kspace/kvirt_area.rs:639`, `ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/mod.rs:2394`, `ostd/src/mm/vm_space.rs:861`
- **Quoted evidence:**

  ```rust
  assert(forall |i: int| (it.pos as int + 1) <= i < it.elements.len() ==>
      CursorMut::<'a, KernelPtConfig, A>::item_slot_in_regions(...))
  by { admit() }

  assert(owner.inv()) by { admit() };

  //*** KNOWN BUG: `self.virt_addr() + len` could overflow. For now, assume that it doesn't. ***
  assume(self.pt_cursor.0.va + len <= usize::MAX);
  ```

  The first `admit()` supplies preservation of the remaining frame-slot obligations after `cursor.map`; the second supplies the cursor invariant immediately before `push_level`. The `assume()` suppresses a stated overflow bug on `CursorMut::unmap`, and the same unchecked addition is then used to compute `end_va`. Consequently, successful verification does not establish these paths from their declared preconditions.

  **Suggestion:** Prove the per-frame preservation fact by carrying uniqueness/remaining-slot facts in the loop invariant; prove `owner.inv()` from the reconstructed continuation and child-owner relations before reinsertion; and replace the overflow assumption with a caller-visible precondition or a checked executable bound that matches the intended API behavior. Do not count these functions as verified until all three gaps are discharged or explicitly authorized and isolated as reviewed trust boundaries.

title: The patch distributes new trusted facts through implementation and model modules
text:
### The patch distributes new trusted facts through implementation and model modules

- **Guideline:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Representative locations:** `ostd/specs/mm/frame/meta_owners.rs:101-119`, `ostd/specs/mm/page_table/cursor/owners.rs:131-166`, `ostd/specs/mm/page_table/node/entry_owners.rs:106-146`, `ostd/src/mm/kspace/mod.rs:388-409`, `ostd/src/mm/page_table/mod.rs:740-773`, `ostd/src/mm/vm_space.rs:1617`
- **Quoted evidence:**

  ```rust
  pub uninterp spec fn is_mmio_paddr(pa: Paddr) -> bool;
  pub broadcast axiom fn axiom_mmio_usage_iff_mmio_paddr(slot: MetaSlotOwner) ...;
  pub axiom fn axiom_mmio_paddr_huge_page_closed(...) ...;

  pub axiom fn make_cont(...) -> (res: Self) ...
  pub axiom fn restore(...) -> (tracked guard: PageTableGuard<'rcu, C>) ...
  pub axiom fn new(...) -> (res: Self) ...

  pub axiom fn axiom_top_level_index_range_bounds<C: PageTableConfig>() ...
  pub axiom fn axiom_leading_bits_only_when_high_half<C: PageTableConfig>() ...
  ```

  These facts are load-bearing for MMIO/allocator disjointness, cursor construction, and address-range reasoning, but they are declared beside their consumers across `ostd/specs` and `ostd/src`. That makes the trusted base difficult to audit and allows application proofs to rely on unchecked structural and hardware-layout claims without a single reviewed boundary.

  **Suggestion:** Move genuinely environmental or executable-model assumptions into a narrow external-spec boundary (with architecture/configuration validity predicates where needed), replace derivable facts with proof lemmas, and make callers import that boundary rather than declaring axioms locally. In particular, prove constructor postconditions from tracked operations wherever possible and restrict the MMIO closure claim to the reviewed architectures/ranges that guarantee it.

title: Non-empty VM copies now reach `unimplemented!()`
text:
### Non-empty VM copies now reach `unimplemented!()`

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`
- **Location:** `ostd/src/mm/io.rs:145` (with the failing primitive at `ostd/specs/mm/virt_mem_newer.rs:429`)
- **Evidence:** Before this change, `memcpy` executed `core::intrinsics::volatile_copy_memory(dst as *mut u8, src as *const u8, len)`. The new body is `VirtPtr::copy_nonoverlapping(&src, &dst, Tracked(mem_src), Tracked(mem_dst), len);`. For every `n > 0`, `copy_nonoverlapping` calls `copy_offset`, which calls `tmp.read(Tracked(mem))`; the newly added executable `VirtPtr::read` body is exactly `unimplemented!()` (`virt_mem_newer.rs:429-439`).
- **Problem:** This is not an executable-preserving packaging change: a non-empty `VmReader::read`/`VmWriter::write` copy follows this path and panics at the first byte instead of copying memory. `#[verifier::external_body]` trusts verification of the body; it does not provide a runtime implementation for `unimplemented!()`.
- **Suggestion:** Restore the original `volatile_copy_memory` executable body and specify that original operation at the trust boundary. If the recursive implementation is intentional, first replace `VirtPtr::read` and `VirtPtr::write` with real runtime byte loads/stores and retain the original implementation/provenance evidence required by `preserve-exec-code`.

title: The claimed `VmSpace` step theorem is proved from duplicate axioms rather than the verified API contracts
text:
### The claimed `VmSpace` step theorem is proved from duplicate axioms rather than the verified API contracts

- **Guidelines:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`, `reuse-existing-specifications`, `complete-external-contracts`
- **Location:** `ostd/specs/mm/vm_space_embedding.rs:179`
- **Evidence:** The new module states that each `_embedded` axiom merely “mirrors the `ensures` clause of one public exec function,” then introduces independent axioms such as `vm_space_new_embedded`, `vm_space_cursor_embedded`, `cursor_mut_map_embedded`, and `vm_space_writer_embedded` (`vm_space_embedding.rs:179-332`). `step` (`:339-365`) calls these axioms, not the actual API specifications. The comment explicitly requires future reviewers to manually update both copies when an exec `verus_spec` changes.
- **Problem:** This creates a second trusted source for facts already expressed by the real API contracts. The resulting `step` theorem establishes preservation for an axiom-defined transition system, not a mechanically connected abstraction of the executable API; contract drift can therefore leave the advertised “soundness theorem” verifying while the real API has different requirements or effects.
- **Suggestion:** Define the embedding transition relation from shared spec predicates used directly by the executable contracts, and prove `step` from verified lemmas over those predicates. Keep unavoidable external facts in the centralized external-spec layer rather than one axiom per local API method.

title: Volatile reads and writes do not expose their value-level effects
text:
### Volatile reads and writes do not expose their value-level effects

- **Guideline:** `api-postconditions`
- **Location:** `ostd/specs/mm/virt_mem_newer.rs:476`
- **Evidence:** `read_volatile<T>` returns `T` but has only `requires` clauses and no `returns`/`ensures` tying the result to the initialized bytes (`virt_mem_newer.rs:476-490`). `write_volatile<T>` promises only that mappings are unchanged and the memory domain can grow (`:511-526`), not that the bytes encode `val`. Its natural caller `VmReader::read_once` returns `Ok(v)` from this value (`ostd/src/mm/io.rs:1298-1335`), yet that public contract likewise constrains only cursor movement, not `v`.
- **Problem:** Callers can prove that an access occurred and ownership advanced, but cannot prove what was read or written. This omits the principal functional promise of these APIs and makes the new memory model unusable for value correctness.
- **Suggestion:** Add a byte encoding/decoding abstraction for `PodOnce`; make `read_volatile` return the decoded bytes and make `write_volatile` update exactly the corresponding byte range while framing the remainder. Propagate the read result guarantee through `read_once`.

title: Centralize the new `core` pointer specification
text: | Centralize the new `core` pointer specification | `upstream-reusable-specs` | `ostd/src/mm/io.rs:87` adds a local `assume_specification` for `<*mut T>::is_aligned`. This models a reusable `core` API rather than an OSTD-specific operation; propose it for the shared/upstream Verus specification layer and consume that definition here. |

title: `nid_to_trace_exec` promises the spec trace but always returns an empty vector
text:
### `nid_to_trace_exec` promises the spec trace but always returns an empty vector

- **Guidelines:** `complete-external-contracts`, `centralize-trusted-boundaries`
- **Location:** `lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/utils.rs:44`
- **Evidence:** The new function is marked `#[verifier::external_body]`, promises `Self::exec_trace_to_ghost(res) =~= NodeHelper::nid_to_trace(nid as NodeId)`, but its complete body is `Vec::new()` (`utils.rs:44-52`). The referenced model returns an empty trace only for the root and otherwise calls `nid_to_trace_rec` (`lock-protocol/src/spec/utils.rs:205-214`). The verified wrapper `nid_to_dep_exec` then returns `trace.len()` (`exec/rw/utils.rs:54-62`), so every legal non-root input executes with depth `0` while its postcondition claims the modeled nonzero depth.
- **Problem:** This is not merely unfinished proof work: the trusted postcondition is false of the executable body. `get_child_exec` consumes the false depth to select a subtree size, so the mismatch can also compute the wrong child ID for non-root nodes while downstream proofs are allowed to assume the specified result.
- **Suggestion:** Implement the actual node-to-trace conversion and verify it, or remove these executable wrappers until that implementation exists. Do not retain `external_body` on a placeholder body with a functional-correctness postcondition.

title: Production allocation and range locking are promoted with their state transitions wholly trusted
text:
### Production allocation and range locking are promoted with their state transitions wholly trusted

- **Guidelines:** `centralize-trusted-boundaries`, `document-real-proof-debt`
- **Locations:** `lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/cursor.rs:274`, `lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/cursor.rs:409`
- **Evidence:** `TransHandler::allocate` is newly annotated `#[verifier::external_body]` and still contains the unresolved exclusivity assertion `assert(prev == INVALID_PADDR) by { admit(); }` (`cursor.rs:274-309`). The public `lock_range` entry point is also newly annotated `#[verifier::external_body]` while advertising strong guarantees including `res.0.wf()`, `res.0.init_wf(*va)`, and a returned model in `WriteLocked` state (`cursor.rs:409-429`). Its body contains multiple admitted facts, including replacing the previous `if pa == INVALID_PADDR { continue; }` behavior with `assert(pa != INVALID_PADDR) by { admit(); }` in the patch.
- **Problem:** The change moves this code out of a test-only module and exposes a production path whose central allocation, exclusivity, termination, and lock-state claims are accepted as axioms at the caller boundary. The trust is distributed in ordinary exec code rather than isolated in a narrowly audited external-specification layer, and the patch provides no safety/trust-boundary statement explaining what establishes the admitted exclusivity and allocation assumptions.
- **Suggestion:** Keep the implementation test-only until these bodies verify, or reduce and isolate the unavoidable trusted primitive behind a narrowly contracted external module. Verify `allocate` and `lock_range` against that primitive, and explicitly document the remaining trusted assumption and why it is sound before promoting the API.

title: `get_child_exec` omits the offset bound required by both its model and implementation
text:
### `get_child_exec` omits the offset bound required by both its model and implementation

- **Guidelines:** `complete-external-contracts`, `api-preconditions`
- **Location:** `lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/utils.rs:64`
- **Evidence:** The public executable helper requires only a valid non-leaf `nid` (`utils.rs:66-68`), but its body immediately trusts `assert(0 <= offset < 512) by { admit(); }` and computes `nid + offset * sz + 1` (`utils.rs:80-82`). The modeled `NodeHelper::get_child` explicitly recommends `0 <= offset < 512` (`spec/utils.rs:266-273`). Since `offset` is `u64`, `0 <= offset` is automatic, but no caller-visible condition excludes `offset >= 512` or arithmetic overflow.
- **Problem:** Any public caller may satisfy the declared preconditions with, for example, `offset == 512` or `u64::MAX`; the implementation's hidden assumption is then false, and its trusted validity/subtree postconditions are unsupported. This is a contract hole rather than a caller restriction: the body itself requires the bound for its documented child-offset model.
- **Suggestion:** Add `offset < 512` (and any arithmetic non-overflow condition not derivable from the node/tree bounds) to `requires`, then verify the implementation. Alternatively make the API fallible for invalid offsets and specify both outcomes.

title: The error import rewrite breaks the VM I/O module
text:
### The error import rewrite breaks the VM I/O module

- **Guideline:** `preserve-exec-code`
- **Locations:** `fvt6-vmreader-and-vmwriter/src/common.rs:4`, `fvt6-vmreader-and-vmwriter/src/io/fallible.rs:5`, `fvt6-vmreader-and-vmwriter/src/io/specs.rs:2`, `fvt6-vmreader-and-vmwriter/src/io/vmrw.rs:3`
- **Quoted evidence:** The patch removes `pub use crate::error::*;` from `common.rs` and removes `error::Error` from `fallible.rs`. In the resulting tree, `fallible.rs:10` still declares `Result<usize, (Error, usize)>` and `fallible.rs:38,107` still use `Error::PageFault`, but that file has no remaining import for `Error`. The patch instead adds `use std::fmt::Error;` to `specs.rs` and `vmrw.rs`; those files still use `Error::PageFault` (`specs.rs:43`, `vmrw.rs:728`) and `Error::InvalidArgs` (`vmrw.rs:136,174,246,526,558,673`). The unchanged crate-local definition at `fvt6-vmreader-and-vmwriter/src/error.rs:9-25` is the enum that actually defines these variants, and its line 5 defines the one-parameter alias `Result<T>` used throughout `vmrw.rs`.
- **Problem:** `fallible.rs` now has an unresolved `Error`, while `specs.rs` and `vmrw.rs` bind `Error` to the formatting error type, which does not define `PageFault` or `InvalidArgs`. Removing the `common::*` re-export also deprives `vmrw.rs` of the crate's `Result<T>` alias, so signatures such as `Result<T>` no longer name the intended API type.
- **Suggestion:** Restore `pub use crate::error::*;` in `common.rs`, or import `crate::error::{Error, Result}` explicitly wherever needed. Remove both `use std::fmt::Error;` additions; do not replace the domain error enum with `std::fmt::Error`.

title: The trusted typed-memory model accepts types that do not satisfy its representation assumptions
text:
### The trusted typed-memory model accepts types that do not satisfy its representation assumptions

- **Guideline:** `restrict-generic-trusted-models`
- **Location:** `ostd/specs/mm/virt_mem.rs:553` (supporting declarations at `ostd/specs/mm/pod.rs:9`, `ostd/specs/mm/pod.rs:77`, and `ostd/specs/mm/pod.rs:86`)
- **Evidence:** `Pod` is declared only as `pub trait Pod: Copy + Sized`, and `PodOnce` only as `pub trait PodOnce: Pod`. Nevertheless, the changed code introduces `pub uninterp spec fn pod_bytes<T: Pod>(val: T)`, a generic injectivity axiom, and a trusted body `#[verifier::external_body] pub fn read_volatile<T: PodOnce>(...) -> (val: T)` whose result is related to arbitrary initialized bytes by `pod_bytes(val) == mem.read_bytes(...)`.
- **Problem:** Neither public safe trait states or enforces that every bit pattern is a valid `T`, that the type has the promised byte model, or that a volatile access is a valid single-instruction operation. A downstream crate can implement these public traits for a local `Copy` type containing restricted-validity fields, so the trusted generic body can perform a typed volatile read from bytes that are initialized but not a valid instance of that type. The new generic model therefore trusts semantic laws that the bound does not establish.
- **Suggestion:** Restrict the trusted surface to audited representations. Seal the traits or make the representation contract an explicit unsafe boundary, add a model-validity predicate admitted only for reviewed type/architecture combinations, and require that predicate on `pod_bytes`, `read_volatile`, and `write_volatile`. Do not expose the generic trusted contract on the strength of `Copy + Sized` alone.

title: `axiom_kernel_mem_view` grants an initialized mapping for any range
text:
### `axiom_kernel_mem_view` grants an initialized mapping for any range

- **Guideline:** `complete-external-contracts`
- **Location:** `ostd/specs/mm/io.rs:49`
- **Evidence:** The documentation says the axiom covers “a kernel-VA range” and appeals to `[KERNEL_BASE_VADDR, KERNEL_END_VADDR)`, but its signature is `pub axiom fn axiom_kernel_mem_view(range: Range<usize>) -> (tracked mv: MemView)` with no `requires`. Its postcondition guarantees a translation, a memory entry, and `Init` for every `va` in the supplied range.
- **Problem:** Any proof caller can pass an arbitrary range and mint a tracked view asserting that every address in it is mapped and initialized. The contract omits the very kernel-range and validity premises used to justify this trust boundary, making the axiom substantially stronger than its rationale and its intended callers require.
- **Suggestion:** Add explicit requirements that the range is well formed, non-overflowing, within the kernel virtual-address interval, and backed by the relevant valid-borrow/mapping premise. Prefer consuming or borrowing an existing permission that establishes initialization instead of creating an unrelated fresh `MemView`; keep this trusted constructor in the centralized external boundary.

title: Three changed functions exceed the permitted `rlimit` cap
text:
### Three changed functions exceed the permitted `rlimit` cap

- **Guideline:** `decompose-before-raising-rlimit`
- **Locations:** `ostd/src/mm/frame/segment.rs:568`, `ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/mod.rs:448`, `ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/mod.rs:1495`
- **Evidence:** Each scoped function has `#[verifier::rlimit(8000)]`; `query` previously used `#[verifier::rlimit(200)]`.
- **Problem:** The VOSTD workflow rule caps scoped `rlimit` values at 200. Each new value is 40 times that cap.
